item.title: Apache Hackathon - 24 August 2019
item.description:
Agenda ¶

ALC Indore invited local Apache enthusiast and open-source lover to participate in the Apache Hackathon.

The participant will contribute to the Apache projects.

The contribution will include, the code development, project documentation, testing and review patches, etc.

The participants who are new to Apache (or open-source) and it’s projects, the ALC Indore will guide them on the ASF, The Apache Way, various Apache Projects, and help them to start their contribution.

item.title: GitHub Workshop
item.description:
Agenda ¶

Acropolis Institute of Technology and Research, Indore has invited ALC Indore team to deliver a GitHub workshop for their students. This workshop will help empower the students to be one step forward into their open source journey as Git and GitHub are important pillars of any open source project. And getting a hands-on exposure early in their careers will be helpful for their future. We aspire to bring in more contributions to the Apache projects by developing interest and awareness in the college students.

item.title: GSoC with the ASF
item.description:
Agenda ¶

GSoC 2023 season has just started and it is a good opportunity to contribute and learn about open source.
ASF has been participating in the event for several years now and will also be participating this year.

This session is targeted towards college students in Indore, to spread awareness about GSoC and guide them through the Apache Way and how the ASF works at large to facilitate participation in the ASF projects for this season.
We aspire to bring in more contributions to the Apache projects by developing interest and awareness in the college students.

item.title: Open Source and ASF Awareness - 15 April 2022

item.title: Open Source and ASF Awareness - 23 November 2019
item.description:
Post Event Report ¶

The ALC Indore successfully organized the “Open Source and ASF Awareness” Session at Indore on 23 November 2019 at Daisy Dales School.

The clicks from the event are available at https://www.flickr.com/photos/alcindore/sets/72157711932233583/

We had a very fruitful and interactive session with bright and young minds, here are highlights from the event.

  • 50+ Students participated in the event and attended the session.
  • The duration for the session was 1 hour 30 minutes including the interaction with the audience.
  • The response from students was overwhelming for us, they asked some surprisingly amazing questions to us, like
    • How can we earn money by making my code open source?
    • Who is the CEO of Apache?
    • If I take an open source project, customize it, and sell it to my friend, can he also sell my customized project.
    • How I can contribute to Apache?
    • How much do you earn by taking these sessions? 😉
    • If a big organization, took my open source project and earn money from it, then will it be my loss?
    • any many more…

After the session, we had a query resolution session in which the students came up with very thoughtful and interesting queries, which we didn’t quite expect considering their age. But they surprised us, most of them seemed to be aware and well-informed even at this young age.

item.title: Open Source and the Apache Way: through a contributor's lens
item.description:
Post-event Report ¶

The event was a huge success. We had 70+ attendees from novice to pro-level developers, students, and others interested in Open Source technologies.

After a wonderful and insightful 1 hour session by Aditya, we had a great Q&A round which went on for another hour.
The audience seemed to enjoy every bit of the knowledge transfer which resulted in the best 2-way communication in a session we have had so far.

item.title: Session on Open Source and Internships opportunities
item.description:
Agenda ¶

It will be an online session where we will have a general discussion about Open source and internship opportunities for the students.
We will cover the following topics in the session, which will be around 1-2 hour long.

1. Introduction to Open Source
2. The Importance of Open Source
3. Benefits of Contributing to Open Source as an Intern
4. Finding Open Source Projects
5. Getting Started with Open Source Contributions
6. Common Challenges & Overcoming Them
7. Internship Programs and Open Source Organisations
8. Success Stories
9. Legal and Ethical Considerations
10. Future Career Prospects
11. Conclusion
12. Q&A Session

item.title: Tech Talk on BigData Infrastructure - 2
item.description:
Post Event Report ¶

Last Friday we organized a tech talk with Joshua Poddoku (Lead Evangelist Apache DevLake) and Jia Fan ( Apache SeaTunnel PPMC) to discuss the popular use cases and where these open-source projects fit into the big data ecosystem.

We hope everyone enjoyed and found value in the delivered content.

This was the second and final session of our “Tech Talk on BigData Infrastructure” series.
The series was aimed to share technical insights on various Apache projects in the big data area, and get contributors and users connected.

item.title: Tech Talk on BigData Infrastructure with Apache DolphinScheduler
item.description:
Post Event Report ¶

We hosted the event via zoom and the registrations were done via Eventbrite https://www.eventbrite.com/myevent?eid=456942807237 and Meetup.com https://www.meetup.com/india-big-data-group/events/289521615/
We got around 15 attendees in the session.

The first half of the session delivered By William was about the different tools used in the BigData infrastructure and what purpose they serve. He later threw light on several case studies where Apache Dolphine Schedular is used.

The second half of the session was delivered by Jay wherein he explained in detail the utility and technicalities related to Apache DolphinSchedular with a great set of examples and an engaging presentation.

item.title: Workshop : The Apache Way 101, April 26, 2021
item.description:

This was altogether a different experience for us, we tried a new variation of events.
Herein we selected a group of dedicated enthusiasts and worked with them for two weeks.

item.title: Workshop on Apache Solr
item.description:
Post Event Report ¶

We were thrilled to receive such an overwhelming response. All our tickets got booked super quickly.
Registrations for the event were done through Eventbrite https://s.apache.org/alc-workshop-solr-event. We used our LinkedIn page and personal LinkedIn accounts for publicity.

The majority of our attendees were college students.

Aditya started with the basic intro about open source and Apache Solr and then we began our show-stopper activity of getting our hands dirty with code with a bit of playing around with how Solr works.
Aditya and our team of volunteers helped the attendees build their first demo application with Apache Solr. We referred to the official tutorial provided on the Apache Solr community for easy access later.
